2.0.5.en: Light settings checks are staggered at startup and retry quietly on transient timeouts.

2.0.4.en: Deploy failures now retry before alerting; notifications only fire after a persistent outage (with a recovery notice), max once per day per i4.

2.0.3.en: Cluster reference light is now the numerically lowest IP (predictable with 3-digit addresses).

2.0.2.en: Switching a cluster on now aligns colour temperature across all its lights, not just brightness.

2.0.1.en: Zone moves now update button scripts instantly (realtime device events); fixed stale device cache.

2.0.0.en: New: HiluX Wall Button driver for the Shelly i4 Gen3. Pair each button, place it in the zone it controls, and the app generates and deploys the i4 script automatically.

1.5.0.en: The app now enforces per-light settings (default fade time, minimum turn-on brightness) and repairs them automatically after firmware updates.

1.4.0.en: Pairing now scans the full /23 around Homey's IP, finding lights on widened (255.255.254.0) networks.

1.3.0.en: Start/stop dimming now use the native CCT.DimUp/DimDown/DimStop of firmware 2.0+, with automatic fallback for older firmware.

1.2.0.en: Added hold-to-dim Flow cards: start dimming (alternating direction) and stop dimming.

1.1.0.en: Added Flow cards: fade to brightness, fade to colour temperature, and wake-up light with smooth transitions.

1.0.1.en: A first attemp to get it so work ...

2.11.0.en: Wall buttons now relay group commands through the app for parallel dispatch — large clusters switch near-simultaneously (local dispatch remains as fallback when Homey is unreachable).

2.11.1.en: New wall buttons now default to dim speed 4 (slightly gentler).

2.11.2.en: Compound gestures accept slower taps (tap window 0.35 s -> 0.55 s).

2.12.0.en: Lamps are hidden from HomeKit automatically; family control goes through the room groups.

2.12.2.en: Wall-button commands re-send to a slow light after 1 s instead of 3 s; relay timing history at :4820/hilux-diag.

2.12.3.en: Group tiles (Homey app, Apple Home) also re-send to a slow light after 1 s instead of waiting up to 8 s.

2.12.4.en: Fade times below 0.5 s (which the lights reject) are raised to 0.5 s instead of silently breaking the button or group.

2.12.5.en: Fade settings accept any value again (e.g. 0.6 or 0.7 s were wrongly refused).

2.13.0.en: Groups can reboot all their lights and buttons (Maintenance action and flow card) so they reconnect to the nearest Wi-Fi access point.

2.13.1.en: i4 button devices are hidden from HomeKit automatically too; only the room groups are exposed.

2.14.0.en: Beta: per-light live connection (WebSocket) - instant brightness/colour state and faster commands, HTTP as fallback.

2.14.1.en: Buttons never switch a room on by guess after a reboot: state check retries and asks a second light; unknown state switches off.

2.14.2.en: Diagnostics page shows when and why each live connection last dropped.

2.15.0.en: Groups have a minimum brightness (default 5 %): sliding to the bottom keeps the room lit instead of switching it off.

2.15.1.en: Switching a group on brings lights left at 0 % up to the group minimum, so they never switch on dark.

2.15.3.en: Wall-button dim floor defaults to 3 %; buttons still on the old 5 % default move to 3 % once.

2.15.4.en: HomeKit hiding only touches devices where the HomeKit experiment is active (preparing for the switch to Matter Bridge).

2.15.5.en: Automatic firmware updates set by the Shelly app are switched off on lights and buttons; updates stay staged.

2.15.6.en: Wall Display panel no longer creates duplicate controls when the display is slow to answer.

2.16.0.en: A group can drive several Wall Displays (comma-separated panel addresses).

2.17.0.en: Multi-room wall dashboard (Living & Kitchen): room tiles with tap-to-toggle and swipe-to-dim; each screen remembers which page it shows.

2.17.1.en: Wall dashboards reload themselves when the app is updated.

2.17.3.en: Wall Display X2 support: answer the Home Assistant app registration so the dashboard loads.

2.17.4.en: Wall Display X2: dashboards report themselves connected to the Home Assistant app, ending the connection-error reloads.
